about: The `$$` block grammar's case list, one file for both authorities that implement it: the editor's lezer extension (mdMath.ts; mdMath.test.ts asserts `editor`) and the server's line pass ahead of comrak (crates/chimaera-server/src/fs.rs promote_math_blocks; its test include_str!s this file and asserts `server` and `reading`). A case added here runs on both sides.
input — the document. Most end with a newline, as a file does; a few end at the closer to pin end-of-document handling.

editor — every math node the live parser yields, in document order, as `containers/Name:source`: Name is InlineMath, DisplayMath (`$$…$$` paired within a paragraph) or MathBlock (a `$$` block; `MathBlock(unclosed)` when its lines ended before a closer); containers are the enclosing block-context nodes (Blockquote, BulletList / OrderedList, ListItem), none at top level. An Escape or Emphasis node would be listed too: no equation may contain one.
server — promote_math_blocks(input), the text comrak then parses; null when the pass leaves the input untouched.
reading — the equations the reading render hands the client, one `style:literal` per `<span data-math-style>` (HTML-escaped, as carried), in document order.

diverges — set, with the reason, on a case the two sides are KNOWN to disagree on. The server test otherwise also requires one closed MathBlock per ```math fence the pass adds: the fixture's own consistency check.

cases.note: a single-line $$…$$ is display math within its paragraph, never a block
three or more dollars are text
fenced code passes through
a fence on a list-marker line passes through too
a raw-HTML block passes through
no closer in sight: prose that merely begins with $$ stays prose
the search for a closer ends at the next blank line
a lazily continued quote is left to inline pairing, like comrak, as long as no later $$ line follows in the paragraph (next case)
a lazily continued quote whose paragraph goes on to another $$ pair
cases.diverges: server: `depth != para_depth` resets the paragraph's $$ parity on the lazy line, so the closing $$ reads as an opener with `y $$ z $$` in sight; comrak alone pairs like the editor

cases.note: a lone $$ line closes display math opened earlier in its paragraph
after that closer the paragraph's next $$ pair is display math again
display math opened mid-line spans several interior lines, backslash-led ones included, with no escapes parsed inside
a lone $$ closer may end the document
a $$ line with a closer in sight is a block, and interrupts a paragraph like a fence
the same equation opened at a line start is a block whose interior is raw
the block closes on the first later line containing $$; text after the closer stays outside it (prose to the server; the editor gives it no node)
a bare punctuation tail after the closer stays outside too
a closer with a tail may end the document
the reported case: a continuation line that would start a bullet list stays inside the equation
a quoted block keeps its > prefix
a tab after > is the quote marker's optional space
a block on a list item's continuation lines keeps its indentation, so it stays in the item
a block on an ordered item's continuation lines (content column 3) stays in the item
a block opened on the marker line keeps the marker and indents its body to the item
a block opened on a marker line whose closer leaves the item (column 0)
cases.diverges: editor: closerAhead checks quote depth only, so the block opens, and the consuming loop ends it unclosed where the closer leaves the item — shown as source; the server re-indents the closer into the item and typesets x

cases.note: a block opened on a marker line whose lines all leave the item (column 0)
cases.diverges: both: the editor ends the block unclosed as `x` leaves the item; the server copies `x` unindented into a fence whose closer it re-indents, and comrak then renders an empty equation, x as prose, and an empty code block

cases.note: a code span's $$ is neither an opener nor a pair toward the paragraph's parity
an unbalanced backtick before $$: the editor and comrak read it as a literal, the server's parity hides the rest of the line
cases.diverges: server: `dollar_pairs` toggles code on every backtick, so the $$ after an unclosed one is not counted; `countDollarPairs` strips only closed spans

cases.note: a heading's $$ does not leak into the next paragraph's parity
a leading YAML frontmatter block is metadata, never math (the editor gates it in mdLive; its parser sees a setext heading, whose $$ does not leak either)
GitHub's ```math fence is the same block under another name: nothing to promote, no math node (mdLive typesets the fence itself), one display equation in reading
content column 4+ (a `10. ` item): the editor knows the column and renders the block; the server leaves it to inline pairing, which the bullet line then cuts
cases.diverges: server: a line pass has no container model, so four or more columns of indentation read as indented code

cases.note: content column 4+ (a nested list item): the same divergence
cases.diverges: server: a line pass has no container model, so four or more columns of indentation read as indented code

cases.note: an autolink takes the $ that follows it on both sides: the URL runs to whitespace, as on GitHub
a superscript run swallows the $ that follows it in the editor; comrak (no superscript extension) parses the math
cases.diverges: editor: the superscript run ^2,$a^ starts before the $ and scans past it

cases.note: a superscript run cannot cross whitespace, so both sides parse the math
